title: Chicken thigh, fried, coated, skin/coating eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken thigh, deep‑fried in a crispy coating, is ready to eat. Both the skin and the breading are edible, giving the dish a rich flavor and texture. The product falls under the pre‑cooked meat category (code 847).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frying at high temperature creates a golden crust that locks in juices.
Thigh meat contains more fat than breast, making it juicier after frying.
The coating is usually made from wheat flour, spices, and sometimes breadcrumbs, adding aroma and crunch.
Such dishes are classic staples of fast‑food and street cuisine worldwide.
When stored properly, the ready‑to‑eat product can last several days in the fridge.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat contains niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6), which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from the meat helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: The fat adds flavor and aids absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium supports fluid balance and heart function.

items.title: High in fat and calories
items.content: Fried meat can contribute to weight gain if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium in the coating
items.content: Salt added to the breading raises sodium intake, which may be undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: If the coating contains wheat flour, people with celiac disease should choose a gluten‑free version.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Improper storage can allow pathogens such as Salmonella to grow.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to eat straight from the package after reheating. It can be served as a main dish, in burgers, salads, with sauces, or as a snack. Adding fresh vegetables or a squeeze of lemon balances the richness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–4 °C in the original packaging or an airtight container. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, though coating quality may decline.
